Then it builds "outbox" powers. x17 = compose(outbox, outbox) i.e. double outbox. x18 = lbind(power, x17): power(x17, n). x16 = interval(1, x15, 1) where x15 = 2 + halve(max(shape)). For 17x17 grid, max=17, halve=8, +2=10, interval(1,10,1) = [1..9]. So powers of double-outbox from 1 to 9.

outbox of a single cell gives the ring around it (3x3 border). Double outbox gives 5x5 border? Let's check: outbox(patch) returns the bounding box expanded by 1. For a single cell at (i,j), outbox = ring at distance 1: cells (i±1, j±1 etc) forming 3x3 border minus center. Actually outbox returns the perimeter lines of the expanded box, so it's the 3x3 ring.

outbox twice: outbox of that 3x3 ring. The patch's bounding box is 3x3, expanded to 5x5, perimeter. So double outbox = 5x5 ring.

power(x17, n) applies x17 n times => rings at size 3+2n. So n=1: 3x3 ring, n=2: 5x5 ring, etc.

Now the algorithm: for each color object, it computes a set of indices (the rings) and the coloring. Let me trace the fancy combinators.
